13: # cli-hermes
14: 
15: > Dispatch a scoped task to Hermes Agent's quiet oneshot chat and return validated code, analysis, or review findings to the calling runtime.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source Python agent CLI, installed as a git checkout under `~/.hermes` and reached through the `hermes` binary. This packet is the seventh mode of the `cli-external-orchestration` hub and makes Hermes available to any runtime that can shell out to it.
22: 
23: The packet owns three things: the routing contract, the availability and provider probes, and prompt construction. It owns no spawn path. Process construction belongs to the shared deep-loop runtime, where `cli-hermes` is the eighth `ExecutorKind` and `buildHermesLineageCommand` emits every dispatch, so a `/deep:research` or `/deep:review` lineage runs on `--executor=cli-hermes` without a packet-local wrapper.
24: 
25: Two traits separate Hermes from the six sibling runtimes, and both shape how you use this mode.
26: 
27: **Hermes has no agent flag.** Its profiles are whole-home islands and its sub-agents receive a goal and context rather than a file, so there is nothing to point at. A persona therefore reaches a session two ways at once:
28: 
29: - The generator mirrors each shared agent as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>`, which carries the whole text.
30: - An environment variable names it, so the repo plugin binds it for the session.
31: 
32: Inlining the persona at the top of the prompt stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror, which keeps every dispatch `{persona + task}` and never a bare task.
33: 
34: **Its repo surface is narrow on purpose.** Hermes reads exactly two things from a project's `.hermes/` folder, `skills/` after a trust grant and `plugins/` behind an opt-in variable. The provider block, shell hooks and MCP servers are user-level config in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` and no repo file can carry them, so they appear here as operator steps.
35: 
36: ### Key Statistics
37: 
38: | Metric | Value |
39: |---|---|
40: | Hub position | Seventh `cli-external-orchestration` mode |
41: | Deep-loop position | Eighth `ExecutorKind`, dispatched by `buildHermesLineageCommand` |
42: | Model roster | Closed at five ids: `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `minimax-m3` and `qwen3.8-max` |
43: | Provider | `llmgateway`, an operator-declared custom provider block |
44: | Agents directory | None. Personas are inlined into the prompt |
45: | Repo surface | `.hermes/skills/`, `.hermes/agents/`, `.hermes/plugins/repo-guards/`, `.hermes/prompts/`, `.hermes/SYNC.md` |
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## 2. QUICK START
50: 
51: ```bash
52: # 1. Probe the binary and the provider. Both must pass before any dispatch.
53: command -v hermes
54: hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url </dev/null
55: 
56: # 2. Dispatch a write task.
57: hermes chat -Q --oneshot --query-file prompt.md --provider llmgateway --model deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
58:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget 840 \
59:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in "$PWD" </dev/null
60: ```
61: 
62: Expected result: the provider probe prints `https://api.llmgateway.io/v1`. The dispatch prints the final response on stdout, `session_id: <id>` on stderr, and exits 0 on success, 1 on a failed result, 130 on an interrupt.
63: 
64: Read the exit code first, then stdout, then stderr. Validate any workspace changes with the repository's code and test gates before handing the result back.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 3. FEATURES
69: 
70: | Feature | What it does |
71: |---|---|
72: | Quiet oneshot dispatch | `chat -Q --oneshot` returns the final response only, with the session id on stderr and hard exit codes. It is the auditable headless form, and `hermes -z` is never used because it drops the session id |
73: | Prompt on stdin | `--query-file -` reads the prompt verbatim from stdin, which is how the fan-out builder passes it. Argv `-q` stays for short prompts |
74: | Read-only review | Omit `--yolo`, narrow the toolset to `-t file,todo` and set `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1` so the repo plugin refuses the write tools; Hermes has no read-only file toolset and no OS sandbox |
75: | Closed model roster | The five ids in `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS` only. `isHermesModelAllowed` rejects any other id in the fan-out, and a manual dispatch must not use one either |
76: | Session isolation | `--ignore-rules` keeps `SOUL.md`, Hermes memories, session search and the CWD instruction files out of the leaf prompt |
77: | Bounded toolsets | An explicit `-t` list excludes `delegation` and `memory`, which the stock roster enables and which would let a leaf spawn sub-agents outside the runner's boundary |
78: | Agent personas | `.hermes/agents/` links the shared agent files and each is mirrored as the skill `agent-<name>`; dispatch with `-s agent-<name>` plus `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA=<name>` (repo plugin), inline otherwise |
79: | Project skills | Every canonical `SKILL.md` mirrored as a generated markdown-only copy under `.hermes/skills/<name>/` (`sync-skills-hermes.cjs`), preloaded with `-s <name>` after `hermes skills trust` |
80: | Project plugin | `.hermes/plugins/repo-guards` bridges the repo's shared guard cores into Hermes hooks, and every hook fails open |
81: | Generated prompt templates | `.hermes/prompts/*.md` mirror `.skilled/commands/**`, regenerated by `sync-prompts-hermes.cjs` |
82: | Self-invocation guard | A Hermes session never dispatches `cli-hermes`. `HERMES_AGENT=true`, `HERMES_SESSION_ID` and process ancestry each refuse the route |
83: 
84: ### The `--yolo` Flag
85: 
86: `--yolo` lifts Hermes's dangerous-action approval gate, the one that covers its dangerous-command patterns such as `rm -rf` and writes whose immediate parent directory is `.hermes`. Headless, no user is present to approve, so a flagged call is denied and the leaf fails on a step it never announced. Ordinary writes and ordinary commands need no flag and run either way.
87: 
88: The rule that follows: a dispatch given a write or terminal toolset passes `--yolo` so a flagged step cannot silently fail it, and a read-only dispatch does not. `--yolo` is an approval bypass, never confinement, so read-only safety is the narrowed `-t` list.
89:

96: | `hermes` binary | On `PATH` | `command -v hermes` gates the route. A missing binary refuses the dispatch before any command is built |
97: | Inference provider | `llmgateway` configured | `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` printing nothing means the route is unusable (`hermes status` does not show custom providers). Report it to the operator |
98: | LLM Gateway credential | `LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY` | Read from `~/.hermes/.env` through the provider block's `key_env` |

20:

24: 
25: Two traits separate Hermes from the six sibling runtimes, and both shape how you use this mode.
26: 
27: **Hermes has no agent flag.** Its profiles are whole-home islands and its sub-agents receive a goal and context rather than a file, so there is nothing to point at. A persona therefore reaches a session two ways at once:
28: 
29: - The generator mirrors each shared agent as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>`, which carries the whole text.
30: - An environment variable names it, so the repo plugin binds it for the session.
31: 
32: Inlining the persona at the top of the prompt stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror, which keeps every dispatch `{persona + task}` and never a bare task.
33: 
34: **Its repo surface is narrow on purpose.** Hermes reads exactly two things from a project's `.hermes/` folder, `skills/` after a trust grant and `plugins/` behind an opt-in variable. 86: `--yolo` lifts Hermes's dangerous-action approval gate, the one that covers its dangerous-command patterns such as `rm -rf` and writes whose immediate parent directory is `.hermes`. 91:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget 840 \
92:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in <repo-root> </dev/null
93: ~~~

96: - `--query-file` reads the prompt verbatim; `-` reads stdin, which is how the fan-out builder passes it. Argv `-q` is for short prompts only.
97: - `--yolo` is required for writes; a read-only dispatch omits it and narrows `-t` to `file,todo`.

143: 6. Use the prompt-quality card's two-tier precedence rule.

145: 8. Keep the current runtime as conductor and Hermes as delegated executor.
146: 9. Treat source-read claims as confirmed only when the contract pin records the live run.
147: 10. Compose every dispatch as `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.

161: 7. Never pass an off-roster model id or a provider-prefixed id.
162: 8. Never pass secrets or provider keys in prompts.
163: 
164: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
165: 
166: 1. Hermes is missing from PATH or `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` prints nothing.
167: 2. The task needs a model outside the closed roster.
168: 3. The task depends on a source-read behavior the contract pin has not yet confirmed.
169: 4. The task requests `hermes skills trust`, `hermes mcp add`, or a config change; those are the operator's.
170: 5. A Hermes plugin or hook would need `--accept-hooks`.

189: - [prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md) - Write, read-only review, generation, and fan-out scaffolds

194: - [Hermes Agent repository](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) - Upstream source and documentation

198: ## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA
199: 
200: ### Dispatch Completion
201: 
202: - Hermes is present on PATH and a provider is configured before launch.
203: - The dispatch carries `--yolo` exactly when it writes, `--ignore-rules` always, and an explicit toolset list.
204: - Exit code, stdout and stderr are all read; `session_id:` is captured from stderr.
205: - Any workspace changes pass the calling workflow's verification gates.
206: - Research and review lineages run through the shared deep-loop runtime.
207: 
208: ### Packet Quality
209: 
210: - References load progressively and stay packet-local.
211: - Source-read behavior is labeled until the contract pin confirms it.
212: - Operator steps (provider, trust, MCP, hooks) are documented as operator steps.
213: - No nested advisor identity is introduced under `cli-hermes`.

217: ## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS
218: 
219: ### Hub Integration
220: 
221: The hub owns advisor identity, mode registration, and router policy. This packet owns only the Hermes workflow contract and must not add `description.json` or `graph-metadata.json`.
222: 
223: ### Deep-Loop Integration
224: 
225: The shared runtime is the sole process adapter. `cli-hermes` is not self-presence exempt: Hermes has in-process delegation, so the ancestry and lockfile guards apply as they do to every kind except Pi.
226: 
227: ### Code and Spec Integration
228: 
229: `sk-code` owns surface detection and code verification. `system-spec-kit` owns Gate 3, spec folders and continuity. Include the parent spec folder in delegated prompts when the workflow has established one.
230: 
231: ### Tool Roles
232: 
233: - Bash runs the availability probe, the provider probe, and the shared runtime entry point.
234: - Read, Glob, and Grep inspect prompts, references, and returned changes.
235: - This packet grants no new external tools.

128: - **A research iteration is slow.** One live fan-out iteration with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` at `max` made thirteen gateway calls on a 65k to 90k token context and finished at 1042 seconds; the `--run-budget` wrap-up notice at 537 seconds was advisory and the runner's ceiling (twice `iterations × timeoutSeconds`) is what binds. Give a `cli-hermes` research lineage `timeoutSeconds` 900 or more.
129: - **`--run-budget` does not bound a stalled provider stream.** Hermes's stale-stream watchdog fires at 600 seconds and retries; the caller's own timeout is the real bound.
130: - **MCP servers are reached only when named in `-t`.** `-t file,todo` hides a configured server; `-t file,todo,code_mode` reaches it.
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ## 4. RULES
135: 
136: ### ✅ ALWAYS
137: 
138: 1. Run `command -v hermes` before every dispatch, and `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` for a configured provider.
139: 2. Delegate research and review lineages to the shared deep-loop runtime. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch runs the dispatch shape in §3 directly.
140: 3. Use `chat -Q --oneshot` with `--query-file`; pass `--yolo` for writes and omit it for read-only work.
141: 4. Pass `--ignore-rules`, `--source tool`, and an explicit `-t` list without `delegation` and `memory`.
142: 5. Keep `--run-budget` under the caller's timeout and read the exit code, then stdout and stderr.
143: 6. Use the prompt-quality card's two-tier precedence rule.
144: 7. Validate Hermes-generated changes with the repository's code and test gates.
145: 8. Keep the current runtime as conductor and Hermes as delegated executor.
146: 9. Treat source-read claims as confirmed only when the contract pin records the live run.
147: 10. Compose every dispatch as `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
148:     - Resolve the persona from the CALLING runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), and INLINE it in the prompt.
149:     - No native persona surface exists: Hermes carries no agent directory of its own, and Hermes profiles are whole-home islands, so `delegate_task` children cannot read agent files.
150:     - Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
151: 11. Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt, copying the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
152: 
153: ### ⛔ NEVER
154: 
155: 1. Never dispatch when `command -v hermes` fails.
156: 2. Never dispatch Hermes from inside Hermes, from inside a fan-out lineage, or when `cli-hermes` already appears in the dispatch stack.
157: 3. Never build a second Hermes adapter inside this packet.
158: 4. Never use `hermes -z` for an auditable dispatch, and never pass `--worktree`.
159: 5. Never run `hermes import-agent`: it copies repo state into the user home and bypasses the trust and quarantine path.
160: 6. Never claim a repo file configures Hermes hooks, MCP servers, or the provider; those are operator steps.
161: 7. Never pass an off-roster model id or a provider-prefixed id.
162: 8. Never pass secrets or provider keys in prompts.
163: 
164: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
165: 
166: 1. Hermes is missing from PATH or `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` prints nothing.
167: 2. The task needs a model outside the closed roster.
168: 3. The task depends on a source-read behavior the contract pin has not yet confirmed.
169: 4. The task requests `hermes skills trust`, `hermes mcp add`, or a config change; those are the operator's.
170: 5. A Hermes plugin or hook would need `--accept-hooks`.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 5. REFERENCES
175: 
176: ### Core References
177: 
178: - [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) - Flags, headless forms, exit codes, isolation flags, environment
179: - [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) - The llmgateway provider contract, the five-id roster, reasoning levels
180: - [hermes-tools.md](./references/hermes-tools.md) - Toolsets, project skills and plugins, the write guard, subsystems that stay off
181: - [integration-patterns.md](./references/integration-patterns.md) - Conductor and executor patterns, cross-validation, anti-patterns
182: - [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) - Persona inlining, persona skills, `delegate_task`, prompt templates for commands
183: - [hook-contract.md](./references/hook-contract.md) - Shell hooks versus the project plugin, the hook map for the repo's guard cores
184: - [mcp-policy.md](./references/mcp-policy.md) - Operator steps for MCP, deny-by-default per tool
185: 
186: ### Templates and Assets
187: 
188: - [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md) - Thin delegator to the canonical prompt-models card
189: - [prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md) - Write, read-only review, generation, and fan-out scaffolds
190: 
191: ### External Sources
192: 
193: - [Research synthesis](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/001-deep-research/research/research.md) - Two-lineage forced-depth research with verified citations
194: - [Hermes Agent repository](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) - Upstream source and documentation
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## 6. SUCCESS CRITERIA
199: 
200: ### Dispatch Completion
201: 
202: - Hermes is present on PATH and a provider is configured before launch.
203: - The dispatch carries `--yolo` exactly when it writes, `--ignore-rules` always, and an explicit toolset list.
204: - Exit code, stdout and stderr are all read; `session_id:` is captured from stderr.
205: - Any workspace changes pass the calling workflow's verification gates.
206: - Research and review lineages run through the shared deep-loop runtime.
207: 
208: ### Packet Quality
209: 
210: - References load progressively and stay packet-local.
211: - Source-read behavior is labeled until the contract pin confirms it.
212: - Operator steps (provider, trust, MCP, hooks) are documented as operator steps.
213: - No nested advisor identity is introduced under `cli-hermes`.
214: 
215: ---
216: 
217: ## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS
218: 
219: ### Hub Integration
220: 
221: The hub owns advisor identity, mode registration, and router policy. This packet owns only the Hermes workflow contract and must not add `description.json` or `graph-metadata.json`.
222: 
223: ### Deep-Loop Integration
224: 
225: The shared runtime is the sole process adapter. `cli-hermes` is not self-presence exempt: Hermes has in-process delegation, so the ancestry and lockfile guards apply as they do to every kind except Pi.
226: 
227: ### Code and Spec Integration
228: 
229: `sk-code` owns surface detection and code verification. `system-spec-kit` owns Gate 3, spec folders and continuity. Include the parent spec folder in delegated prompts when the workflow has established one.
230: 
231: ### Tool Roles
232: 
233: - Bash runs the availability probe, the provider probe, and the shared runtime entry point.
234: - Read, Glob, and Grep inspect prompts, references, and returned changes.
235: - This packet grants no new external tools.
236: 
237: ---
238: 
239: ## 8. REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES
240: 
241: The router discovers markdown resources dynamically. Start with the CLI reference and prompt-quality card, then load only the references matching the task. Use [prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md) for repeatable prompt construction.
242: 
243: Related skills: cli-opencode, cli-claude-code, cli-codex, cli-cursor, cli-devin, and cli-pi for sibling CLI dispatch; sk-code for code standards; system-deep-loop for execution; system-spec-kit for packet handback.

13: 
14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320:

322:

327: 2. [Action 2]
328:

332:

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation

341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right

363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues

372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |

383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison

388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

15: # Hermes Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: This reference prevents a category error: Hermes profiles and `delegate_task` sub-agents are not persona surfaces for this repo's agents.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Records every route a repo persona can take into a Hermes dispatch, and the reason a profile or a `delegate_task` child cannot stand in for one.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Composing a dispatch that carries a resolved agent persona
28: - Deciding whether to preload `agent-<name>` or inline the persona
29: - Checking what a `delegate_task` child may and may not do
30: - Finding the prompt template for a nested `.skilled/commands` command
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. PERSONA ROUTES
39: 
40: | Route | Works | Use when |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | Inline the persona block at the top of the prompt, after the child-dispatch preamble | Yes | Default; the `cli-codex` and `cli-pi` precedent |
43: | Persona skill preloaded with `-s <name>` from `./.hermes/skills` | Yes, after the trust grant | Only if prompt size becomes a measured problem; needs the repo-local folder and the operator's trust |
44: | `hermes profile create` per agent | No | Profiles isolate homes and credentials, not personas |
45: | `hermes import-agent claude-code` | No | Imports `CLAUDE.md` into memories and copies skills into the user home; never imports agent files; bypasses trust and quarantine |
46: 
47: Resolve the persona from the calling runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), since Hermes has none of its own and its personas travel inlined in the prompt, and map each subtask to the right agent (code, review, design, deep-research, markdown). The canonical contract is `../../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. COMMANDS
52: 
53: The repo's nested commands under `.skilled/commands/**` have no Hermes equivalent: Hermes has no workflow engine and its slash commands are its own. The cli-pi precedent applies: flatten each command into a prompt template under `.hermes/prompts/` and carry it with `--query-file`. A sync script generates those templates; a dispatch loads the template text into its prompt file.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 4. PERSONA THROUGH THE REPO PLUGIN
58: 
59: `.hermes/agents/` links the shared runtime-neutral agent files, and `sync-skills-hermes.cjs` mirrors each as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>` because Hermes has no agent flag and caps a plugin prompt section at 4000 characters (a 22k persona in a section was skipped outright).
60: 
61: The native-shaped dispatch pairs:
62: 
63: - `-s agent-<name>`, the skill that carries the whole persona
64: - `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA=<name>`, the name the plugin's persona section binds for the session
65: 
66: `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` must be set for the plugin to load.
67: 
68: `--ignore-rules` is passed alongside `-s`: a live A/B under the flag showed the preload still reaching the model, so omitting it only bled SOUL.md, memories and session search into the leaf. Inline stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 5. SKILLS
73: 
74: With the repo trusted, Hermes loads the curated per-skill links under `.hermes/skills/<name>` and can preload one with `-s <name>` (observed 2026-09-14: `-s cli-hermes` quoted the packet's first hard rule). A dispatch that needs any other skill names it in the prompt by path, because only linked skills are visible to Hermes and the hub identity does not cross the link.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 6. `delegate_task` AND THE DELEGATION BOUNDARY
79: 
80: Hermes's own sub-agents are spawned by the `delegation` toolset. A leaf lineage never carries that toolset: a sub-agent spawned inside a lineage runs outside the runner's containment and stack guards. For non-leaf use, the semantics of `delegation.subagent_auto_approve`, child timeouts and flag inheritance are open questions for the contract pin. Because Hermes has in-process delegation, `cli-hermes` is not exempt from the self-presence guards the way `cli-pi` is.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 7. MCP AND HOOKS AS DELEGATION SURFACES
85: 
86: MCP servers are user-level ([mcp-policy.md](./mcp-policy.md)); the repo's guard cores reach a Hermes session through the project plugin ([hook-contract.md](./hook-contract.md)). Neither is a persona surface.

14: 
15: # cli-hermes Providers, Models & Invocation
16: 
17: The single catalog of the provider, the model ids, the reasoning lever and the dispatch shape the cli-hermes mode can reach. Hermes is a multi-provider pass-through with a catalog of some forty providers; this mode deliberately reaches one of them.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: One place to answer "which provider, which model, which effort, how to dispatch" for cli-hermes.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Choosing the `--provider` and `--model` pair for a `hermes chat` dispatch.
30: - Mapping a reasoning effort onto `--reasoning`.
31: - Configuring, as the operator, the provider block Hermes needs.
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: The roster is closed at five ids so generic provider routing cannot broaden dispatch, and the provider is the one whose credential the operator already holds for the other runtimes.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. THE PROVIDER CONTRACT
40: 
41: Hermes resolves `--provider NAME` against its built-in providers or a user-defined block under `providers:` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. The LLM Gateway (DevPass) is not a built-in, so the operator declares it. The packet pins the block's name and key variable, because the runtime's builder passes `--provider llmgateway` and its env allowlist passes the `LLMGATEWAY_` prefix:
42: 
43: ```yaml
44: providers:
45:   llmgateway:
46:     base_url: https://api.llmgateway.io/v1
47:     key_env: LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY
48: ```
49: 
50: The key itself lives in `~/.hermes/.env` or the shell; it never appears in a prompt, a repo file, or this skill's files. This is an operator step: no dispatch, plugin or repo file writes it. The field names were confirmed live on 2026-09-14 (`hermes config set providers.llmgateway.base_url ...` and `.key_env`); the shape above follows Hermes's `custom` provider convention (source-read: `cli-config.yaml.example`, `hermes_cli/config_providers.py`).
51: 
52: Other credential kinds on this machine do not transfer: Hermes keeps its own OAuth sessions in `~/.hermes/auth.json`, and its Codex import reads `~/.codex/auth.json` once at login rather than sharing it. A Codex OAuth import is a possible second provider later; it is not on this roster.
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. THE ROSTER
57: 
58: | Model id | Provider | Reasoning | Standing | Notes |
59: |---|---|---|---|---|
60: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | `llmgateway` | pinned `max` | **observed 2026-10-22**: a live fan-out dispatch with no model pinned built `--model deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` and replied `OK` | The rotation default; the same literal cli-pi dispatches through DevPass |
61: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `llmgateway` | pinned `max` | **observed 2026-09-14**: smoke exit 0, fan-out lineage dispatched | The 2026-09-10 release, still selectable and pinnable; llmgateway's DeepSeek provider route for it is Deactivating on Oct 24, 2026, so a pinned run must move to the `-1017` id before then |
62: | `glm-5.3-flash` | `llmgateway` | pinned `max` | **observed 2026-09-14**: smoke exit 0 at `max` and `none` | The second lens; flat-price on DevPass |
63: | `minimax-m3` | `llmgateway` | the caller's effort | probed live on this route, per `SKILL.md` | In `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS` and its fan-out mirror |
64: | `qwen3.8-max` | `llmgateway` | the caller's effort | probed live on this route, per `SKILL.md` | In `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS` and its fan-out mirror |
65: 
66: Every id is a bare gateway literal. A provider-prefixed form (`llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash`) is Pi's selector shape, not Hermes's, and the fan-out rejects it. Enforcement: `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS` and `isHermesModelAllowed` in `executor-config.ts`, byte-mirrored as `HERMES_ALLOWED_MODELS` in `fanout-run.cjs`; no `auto` default exists.
67: 
68: To add a model: amend the mode's spec, then `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS`, its mirror, this table and the changelog, in that order.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 4. REASONING LEVELS
73: 
74: - **Accepted set:** `--reasoning` accepts `none minimal low medium high xhigh max ultra`, the same set as the runtime's `REASONING_EFFORTS`, so the builder forwards the effort without a map.
75: - **Fan-out pin:** every Flash-family roster model is a reasoning model the runtime pins to `max` (`isFlashMaxPinnedModel`); a lower requested effort never reaches Hermes from the fan-out.
76: 
77: A direct dispatch may pass any level; observed 2026-09-14 through the gateway:
78: 
79: | Model | Level | Result |
80: |---|---|---|
81: | `glm-5.3-flash` | `max` | exit 0, `OK`, 17 s |
82: | `glm-5.3-flash` | `none` | exit 0, `OK`, 17 s |
83: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `low` | exit 0, `OK`, 21 s |
84: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `ultra` | exit 0, `OK`, 24 s |
85: 
86: No level was refused. Exit 0 shows the gateway accepted the level, not that the model honored it; `minimal`, `medium`, `high` and `xhigh` were not sent.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## 5. INVOCATION
91: 
92: ```bash
93: hermes chat -Q --oneshot --query-file <prompt.md> --provider llmgateway --model deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
94:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget 840 \
95:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in "$PWD" </dev/null
96: ```
97: 
98: Fan-out: `--executor=cli-hermes --model=glm-5.3-flash` on `/deep:research` or `/deep:review`; the runtime builds the command.
99: 
100: ---
101:
